scope: Independent endpoint representation assessment only; no owner, maintained repository, Git or GitHub mutations
decision: Retaining the issued pyochelin-I monoanion is defensible as the explicitly limited native reaction projection of one experimentally observed end-product stereoisomer. This is not an assertion of exclusive I biosynthesis, I-selective enzymatic release, an intracellular I/II ratio, or exact equivalence to a neutral compound/class.

checks: Original CPD-9992 InChI is the I configuration and has net charge -1; neutralization matches CHEBI:67183 exactly.
CHEBI:29669 has net charge zero and leaves the interconverting thioaminal stereocenter unspecified; chirality-aware matching contains neutral I and II.
CHEBI:67183 and CHEBI:67185 are distinct stereoisomers, not exact chemical identities.
Neutralized MetaCyc:CPD-12093 is enantio-pyochelin and is not a member of the P. aeruginosa I/II class.
limits: No arbitrary InChI sign was interpreted as an R/S descriptor; the molecular graph was decoded independently.
Acid/base normalization is a derived comparison, not an exactMatch assertion or silent replacement of native reaction forms.

primary_evidence.scope: Original publisher full text, web inspected; no local original-body SHA claimed
locators: Results: PchG is required for pyochelin formation in vitro; Figure 2
Methods: Production and detection of salicylate-containing compounds
primary_evidence.assessment: The reconstituted products match I/II chromatographic peaks and masses of the natural standard. Products were analyzed after acidification/extraction, and displayed peaks were normalized. These observations establish recovered I/II products, not release stereoselectivity or a physiological ratio.

primary_evidence.scope: Original indexed abstract, also retained Europe PMC original XML; full paper not claimed
primary_evidence.assessment: The abstract specifies interconvertible P. aeruginosa I and II configurations and distinguishes the P. fluorescens CHA0 enantio-pyochelin mixture. It supports stereochemical interpretation, not transferring CHA0 biosynthesis to PAO1.

primary_evidence.scope: Original full article and SI PDFs independently re-extracted; article pages 8/9 and SI pages 2/16/17 independently rendered and visually inspected
primary_evidence.locator: Article Methods p.9; Supplementary Figure 1 p.2, Figure 15 p.16 and Figure 16 p.17
primary_evidence.assessment: The pathway figure is a biosynthetic schematic. The reported PchD/PchE/SrfD reconstitution releases upstream salicylate-cysteine intermediates; it does not directly assay full PchF/G terminal I-selective release. No terminal stereoselectivity is transferred from the drawing.

representation_requirements: Keep all eleven native member objects, the complete terminal release, and the declared salicylate-start boundary; do not substitute an early fragment.
Keep the explicit I/II and release-selectivity limits in the pathway and terminal-edge descriptions.
Treat the terminal I equation/net as native formal end-member bookkeeping, not a measured product ratio.
Do not mint an epimerization reaction, relabel enantio-pyochelin, or claim neutral-class equivalence.
A broader neutral CHEBI:29669 alternative would need explicit changed acid/base bookkeeping and native mapping qualification; endpoint evidence does not require that replacement.

source_locality_recommendation.observation: The InChI locator supports structure; the same block also contains an experimentally observed I/II and curator-projection statement. The separate primary evidence and description already ground/qualify that interpretation.
source_locality_recommendation.recommendation: Keep this native block literal, or clearly label the I assignment as a derived comparison. Keep I/II observations and the chosen projection in their primary evidence/description. Prefer experimentally observed I/II products where no intracellular equilibrium or ratio was measured.

remaining_scope: Complete record identifiers, all other edges, exact construct/sequence bridges, assemblies, full schema/KGX and final independent scientific review remain separate. This endpoint assessment does not certify the unfinished record.
